name: songs-surface-merge
note: SONGS-MERGE phase 1 (decisions.md SONGS-MERGE; systems/songs-surface-merge.md). Library and Setlist were two bottom-nav tabs listing the same records, so nothing said which one was the truth about a song - the operator reported exactly that confusion. They are ONE 'Songs' surface now with an All | Setlist segmented switch, per component-conventions:65 (bottom nav = top-level surfaces ONLY; view switches are segmented). The load-bearing goalpost is #1: a row's affordances derive from setlist MEMBERSHIP, not from which view you are standing in, so an in-set song shows its position in the All view too. Red-first: every goalpost below fails on the pre-merge two-tab build.

steps.label: layout settle gate: fonts loaded before any geometry is measured
RED GOALPOST (structure): the bottom nav no longer carries a separate Setlist tab - one collection is one surface
the Songs surface owns an All | Setlist segmented switch, and it opens on All (operator ruling: never a state-dependent landing)
the Setlist segment carries a count badge, so 'is there anything in my set?' is answerable without switching

RED GOALPOST 1 (the load-bearing one): an in-setlist song shows its POSITION in the ALL view - affordances derive from membership, not from which view you are standing in. Pre-merge this was only knowable by switching tabs

an in-set row keeps the CHECK-MARK toggle in the All view - not the setlist's red remove handle. In a list of ALL songs a red x reads as 'delete this song', not 'take it out of tonight's set': the same glyph means different things depending on what the list IS. And no grip - a drag in a searched, sorted list would reorder against an order that is not on screen
a song NOT in the setlist still offers the + (the two states are visibly different in one list)
RED GOALPOST 2: the Setlist segment swaps the CHROME wholesale - search and filters go (a setlist is hand-ordered, not searched), the set head row arrives
RED GOALPOST 4: Start performs the setlist from the Setlist segment header, where it has always been
the setlist rows keep their full grammar here - position, grip AND remove - because in this view the order IS the content
RED GOALPOST 5: every visible control on the Setlist view clears the 44px tap floor (offset metrics - the rect is the transformed box and these controls carry :active scales)
RED GOALPOST 3: switching back does not disturb the other view's state - the set still has both songs, in order, and the All chrome is back
taking a song OUT of the set from the All view works through its check-mark toggle, and the badge follows without a view switch
the removal landed: one song left in the set, and the segment badge says so without a view switch
